exposure: Infant diet (predominantly or exclusively breastfeeding, introduction of solid foods, weaning)
outcome: Abundance and prevalence of specific bacterial species (e.g., Bacteroides, Bifidobacterium)
cohort: The study profiled 698 stool samples from 84 predominantly or exclusively breastfed infants in the BLOSOM cohort.
finding: Breastfeeding may buffer early-life gut microbiome perturbations, while diet transitions, such as the introduction of solid foods, exert major and lasting effects on gut microbiome composition and diversity.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with transient reductions in Bacteroides abundance and prevalence, but did not affect Bifidobacterium abundance.
